opening_lines: S(n) numbers a derivational stage. It does not number a simplex dimension. At stage zero, <> is one opaque whole. Supplying that inscription leaves the admitted regime empty. A supplied mark admits nothing.
At stage one, <a> is one opaque token. Supply of that mark is a no-op. Admission is a later explicit event. The stage index is not a point, and it is not a one-dimensional simplex.

At stage two, reading L retains the opaque wholes <a> and <ab>. The inscription <ab> is not a pair inside the regime. Glyph identity, component count, and order are unavailable. A later grammar may parse the same bytes as two glyphs. That parser is a new interpretation, not the source token.

Stage three asks those two opaque data to be separable under a stated item cost. That cost does not force a triangular face. A stage is not a triangle. A simplicial complex can be supplied later as a realization, and a realization has no authority to create the next stage.

## What kind of rewrite is being proposed?
| Kind | Required question | What the result can establish |
| Representation | Can the declared decoder recover the original carrier and orientation? | A round trip on the specified domain; no automatic improvement in reasoning. |

| Cochain repair | Is the change exactly `d0*a` under the fixed maps? | The same quotient class; the optimal quotient obstruction is preserved. |
| Problem change | Were the carrier, edge observations, norms, maps or assumptions changed? | A different problem, requiring separate provenance and evidence. |
